evidence.clarity: The H1 'Too lumpy today?' is the group-chat question, not a description. The lede gets there: 'reads the tide, wind, swell and water temperature at your beach and shows the windows... One look on the way down, in the dark, before work.' The fact that it is an iPhone app only appears in the grey cta-note 'iPhone. 40 beaches...'. A swimmer can repeat it after the lede, not from the headline.
evidence.fit: The tone fits the brief: night-water palette, bands that lighten 'as the morning goes on', 'half five', 'Which gloves?'. The 'Conditions, not permission' band says 'It will never tell you it's safe to swim', and the lock-screen notification shows the early-close warning. Beta URL, iPhone and 40 beaches are all used correctly. The not-a-lifeguard message sits four bands down and not inside the hero readout.
evidence.distinctiveness: The tide-line hero that draws in, a group-chat bubble set beside 'four tabs', an iPhone lock screen at 05:42 with a Tidewise notification, and a page that brightens from night to grey morning. With the logo removed you would still recognise it as a sea-swimming product. No stock card grid.
evidence.proof: The hero chart is operable. I dragged the range from 05:00 to 10:20 and dragged the chart itself to 08:40. The status moves through 'Window opens at 06:20', 'In the window until 08:00', 'Window closed early at 08:00. Last night it ran to 09:10' and 'No window for the rest of the morning'. The figures match the beach rows (06:20 to 08:00) and the notification (closes 08:00, ran to 09:10). At 1440 the readout and slider are below the fold (caption at y=1276). The wind directions contradict each other: SW is 'offshore' but NW is 'onshore' at the same beach, and a regular swimmer would notice.
evidence.craft: Restrained type (light sans display, Charter body) and a consistent palette. At 1440 the first screen leaves the right half empty beside the headline, and the chart starts at y~630. axe reports 1 serious colour-contrast node at 390 and 1440. The status reads '1 h 0 min' at 07:00.
evidence.mobile: At 390 the first screen shows the headline, lede, 'Join the public beta' and the chart with '06:10 now' and '06:20 to 08:00 swim window'. Nothing overflows (probe 0px at 320/390). The 'lost to the wind' label is hidden by display:none at <=520px, so on a phone the hero's hatched early-close area has no label. The range input is 28px tall, and the header 'Join the beta' link is 40px. The status readout starts below the fold.
evidence.honesty: The hero chart says '06:10 now', which reads as live. Its label 'A made-up November morning at an example beach... Not a forecast.' sits below the readout, at y=1160 at 390 and y=1276 at 1440, so it is out of view on the first screen at both widths. The lock-screen notification has no visible example label (only an aria-label). The beach rows are labelled 'Example beaches and times.' The CTA 'Join the public beta' goes to the brief's URL. The safety disclaimer is clear and is repeated in the footer.
evidence.interaction: The range input and pointer-drag on the chart both work at 1440/768/390, and the status is aria-live with four distinct states. There are no console errors. There is no reset and no labelled snap points. The 28px slider is the only visible control. 'Drag through the morning' is the only affordance, and it is below the fold at 1440. There is no menu, which is fine since the header has a single link.
evidence.copy: Specific and written in the swimmer's own world: 'Four tabs and a group chat, at half five', 'Is there enough water over the rocks yet?', 'Which gloves?', 'Conditions, not permission', 'It won't nudge you to go in. It tells you what changed.' I found no buzzwords. Two small defects: the generated '1 h 0 min', and the onshore/offshore direction mismatch in the readout.
evidence.first_screen: At 1440 the screen shows the slogan headline, the lede, the CTA, and only the top of the chart with the '06:20 to 08:00 swim window' and 'lost to the wind' labels. There is no example label, no readout, and a large empty area to the right. At 390 it shows the headline, CTA and chart with '06:10 now', again with no example label in view. The promise is specific only in the lede, and the chart that would make it believable is unlabelled.

problems: The hero chart reads as live ('06:10 now') and its 'made-up morning... Not a forecast' label is out of view on the first screen at both 390 and 1440. A swimmer wary of being told it is safe meets a window before she meets the disclaimer.

The readout and controls are below the fold at 1440, and on a phone the early-close label is hidden, so the hero never shows the 'warns when a window closes early' promise without scrolling or dragging.
Wind directions contradict each other (SW is offshore, yet NW is onshore at the same beach). There are also small finish issues: '1 h 0 min', a 28px slider, and the empty right half of the 1440 hero.

evidence.clarity: The H1 'Check the sea, not the group chat' and the lede 'Tidewise is an iPhone app for people who swim in the sea all year. It turns the tide, wind, swell and water temperature at your beach into today's swim windows, and warns you when one closes early.' say what it does, who it is for and what the action is. The button reads 'Join the iPhone beta', and the note under it says 'Opens the beta page.'
evidence.fit: Every ask is met: iPhone, public beta, 40 UK and Ireland beaches, the brief's URL on all CTAs, and the early-close warning in the hero. Under 'What only you can read' it lists flags, rips, and 'How much cold you can take today'. The not-a-lifeguard tension is resolved inside the artifact itself ('Conditions, not a verdict. You decide whether to swim.' under every readout). The pre-dawn palette fits, but the four-strip chart section leans toward the weather-dashboard feel the brief warned against.
evidence.distinctiveness: The tide-curve hero has sunrise and sunset ticks and hatched 'was 08:30' bands. There is also a south-facing cove plan with offshore and onshore arrows, a cove cross-section with a swimmer and tow float, and before/after window bars. Everything comes from the product, but the structure is a familiar hero plus demo plus sections, and the strips chart reads like a forecast site.
evidence.proof: The core job is operable on the first screen at 1440. The chart, the readout ('Inside the morning window, 1 h 30 min left. Closes early today at 07:30... overnight forecast said 08:30') and the 06:00/07:00/08:00/17:00 chips are all visible. The numbers agree across the hero, the strips, the 'Overnight forecast 05:30-08:30 / This morning 05:30-07:30' bars and the readout. The wind directions match the stated south-facing beach (N offshore, SW onshore), and the cove plan explains it.
evidence.craft: A deliberate Lora/Inter scale with consistent spacing, and axe is clean at 390 and 1440. At 1440 the hero chart's 'Morning window 05:30-07:30' label runs past the band into the hatch, and 'Closes early: was 08:30' crowds the sunrise chip. That one cluttered corner aside, I found no defects at 1440, 768 or 390.
evidence.mobile: At 390 the first screen holds the headline, lede, CTA, 'Sample day... Not a forecast.' label and the recomposed chart (short labels 05:30-07:30, 'was 08:30'). Chips and range are 44px, nothing overflows, and the menu opens. Tapping 'Not a lifeguard' scrolled to the section and closed the menu, and Escape closes it. After tapping a chip, the chart marker moves in view, but the verdict readout sits about 200px below the chips.
evidence.honesty: 'Sample day at a sample south-facing beach, written for this page. Not a forecast.' sits directly above the chart at every width. The verdict wording is 'Inside/Outside the windows', never safe. Every readout ends with 'Conditions, not a verdict. You decide whether to swim.' The CTA note says 'Opens the beta page' before the click. The cove drawing is captioned 'Illustration'. There are no reviews or numbers beyond the brief.
evidence.interaction: I tried all four chips, the range at 05:00, 07:45, 11:40, 20:00 and 21:00, and Reset at 1440, 768 and 390. Each change updated the time, light ('Dark until sunrise at 07:24' / 'After sunset'), verdict, early-close line and values. The end state reads 'No more windows in this sample day', and Reset re-checks the 06:00 chip. The verdict is role=status. The menu toggles, closes on link and on Escape. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific and consistent: 'Pick when you'll reach the beach', 'Arriving at', 'Reset to 06:00', 'One hour of the window is gone', 'Flags and lifeguard advice, where your beach has them'. Every button says what happens. Some paragraphs are explanatory and long ('Each strip below is something you used to look up on its own...'), and the voice is plainer than a 6 am mood.
evidence.first_screen: At 1440 one viewport holds the outcome for a named audience ('people who swim in the sea all year... warns you when one closes early'), a labelled sample chart with a live readout showing an early close, and 'Join the iPhone beta' with 'Opens the beta page.' At 390 the promise, CTA, sample label and window chart with 'was 08:30' are all in view.

problems: The four-strip 'one line' chart and data-dense hero lean toward the weather-app look the brief asked to avoid. It is accurate, but the page is less of a 6 am mood than a well-made forecast explainer.
On a phone the verdict readout sits below the arrival chips, so the main feedback after a tap is just below the fold (only the chart marker moves in view).
At 1440 the hero's top-left labels collide: 'Morning window 05:30-07:30' runs into the hatched area, and 'Closes early: was 08:30' crowds the sunrise chip.

reason: Reading as the swimmer in the car park: B tells me exactly what I'm getting, labels the sample before I see it, and puts 'Conditions, not a verdict. You decide whether to swim.' inside the readout I'm operating. That answers my first doubt where I look. A has the better voice and mood, but its '06:10 now' chart reads as live with the example label far below, and its wind directions don't add up. As the founder I'd ship B tomorrow. A would win if it moved the example label and the not-a-lifeguard line into the hero and fixed the wind directions.
